task: ops status reported the wrong Track 1 mode after the operator started track1-only

root_cause.what: a rename boundary, one field wide
chain: scan_processes maps that field onto a dataclass attribute named `command`
track1_status asked for `CommandLine` - the name on the FAR side of the boundary - and got None
root_cause.why_silent: None became '', and an empty string contains no flags, which parses as legacy-only. Searching an empty string is a perfectly successful operation, so nothing raised and nothing looked wrong
root_cause.symptom: with the scheduler genuinely running --track1-only-shadow, status printed track1_mode=legacy-only and track1_safety_routes=['legacy']
root_cause.why_no_test_caught_it: the Stage 5K status test builds its fixture with the key CommandLine - the key the BUGGY READER wanted, not the key the producer emits. Test and bug agreed with each other; production disagreed with both

monitor/ops.py: new process_command(proc): reads `command`, falls back to `CommandLine` - one home for the key, with the rename boundary documented
new scheduler_command_lines(procs=None): the single joiner, so a second consumer cannot reintroduce the key mistake independently

scheduler_track1_shadow now answers 'are the Track 1 slots registered' (track1_only implies it in make_scheduler) instead of 'is this literal flag on the argv'; the literal flag kept as scheduler_track1_shadow_flag
typing import extended with Mapping, Sequence (the annotations are evaluated)
files_changed.scratch/test_track1_stage5m_d_track1_onl: the cmd_up test now redirects TRACK1_LEDGER_DIR/TRACK1_TELEMETRY_DIR to tmp_path
files_changed.scratch/test_track1_stage5k_ops_startup_: the runtime-root guard re-pointed: it asserted ABSENCE, which is wrong once an operator has legitimately started a session

second_finding.what: global_index/track1_runtime/ was created by MY OWN Stage 5O mutation harness
second_finding.when: 2026-08-24 00:28:17 - before the operator's scheduler start at 02:08:42
second_finding.how: the D4 mutation deliberately neuters cmd_up's both-flags refusal; the un-refused cmd_up then ran TRACK1_LEDGER_DIR.mkdir(parents=True) against the real tree
second_finding.lesson: a test whose safety depends on the code under test taking an early return leaks the day someone deliberately removes that return
second_finding.state: two EMPTY directories; no evidence files were written by any test
second_finding.not_deleted: the running track1-only scheduler now depends on them - window_ledger refuses when its directory is not a dir, so deleting them would make every slot hard-refuse ledger_not_configured and destroy the live shadow session's evidence collection
second_finding.fixed_at_source: the cmd_up test redirects both dirs to tmp_path, so even a mutated cmd_up cannot reach the real ones
